recent_videos.title: How the World Is Stripping Kids of Their Agency | Shiv Tandan
recent_videos.description:
"Ghar jaake light off kar dena" is not the solution to an apocalypse.  
​We are raising a generation with massive idealism
kids who want to end world hunger and poverty but who rate their own sense of power at a 2 out of 10. Even the most privileged kids feel like they have zero control over their own futures.  

​If we want to fix education, we have to stop teaching passive obedience and start building real-world agency.  
​Want to see how we can actually give kids their power back?

recent_videos.title: Give Children Agency and They Will Change the World | Shiv Tandan
recent_videos.description:
What is school actually for?

At the Critical Thinking Un-Conference, Shiv Tandan explores the heavy mental landscape of young students today—from climate anxiety and AI to the endless pressure of exams and competition.

Instead of adding more expectations onto teachers and students, Shiv breaks down how to move past a passive education system. Learn about the cycle between knowledge and action, why building student agency is vital, and how practical tools like the "V for Very Good" framework can help us rethink modern schooling. 

Key Topics Covered: 
● Why modern students face a growing loss of agency and high-pressure environments. 
● The missing bridge between theoretical knowledge and real-world action. 
● How to balance self-knowledge and world knowledge using simple frameworks.

recent_videos.title: Stop Putting AI in Classrooms Just Because You Can | Shiv Tandan
recent_videos.description:
Every new technology in education comes with a promise.

But before we ask “How do we use AI in the classroom?” maybe we should ask something much simpler:
What problem are we actually trying to solve?

Education already has problems worth solving curiosity, critical thinking, pressure, teacher workload.

If AI doesn't meaningfully address those problems, why are we rushing to put it everywhere?

Technology should serve education. Not the other way around.

What do you think - what problem should AI actually solve in education?

recent_videos.description:
Won’t they become weird and friendless?

It’s one of those questions people ask about homeschooling almost as if social skills only happen at school.

But children build friendships and learn how to navigate people in far more places than a classroom.

Day 6 of my Homeschooling FAQ.

recent_videos.title: Stop Replacing Your Child's Dreams With Your Expectations | Ft. Nikita Tomar Mann
recent_videos.description:
Sometimes, without even realising it, we start building a future for our children that looks more like our dream than theirs.

We call it guidance. We call it wanting the best for them.

But somewhere along the way, are we still listening to what they want?

A thought worth sitting with.

What do you think parents should do when a child's dream looks completely different from what they had imagined?

recent_videos.title: Can Both Parents Work Full-Time & Still Homeschool? | Homeschooling FAQ 05 | Shiv Tandan

These are the questions that really matter when homeschooling stops being an idea and starts becoming a possibility.

So here's Part 2 of my Homeschooling FAQ.

recent_videos.title: 90% of your child’s brain develops before age 7—are you giving them your time or just a screen?
recent_videos.description:
What is the most important phase in your child's life? 

Many parents assume it's during their 10th standard, 12th standard, or college years. But research tells a completely different story. The most critical period for shaping a human being is actually from birth to 7 years old.   In this insightful episode of Parenting Hacks with Meghna, we explore why early childhood is the foundation for your child's entire future. During the first 7 years, 90% of a child’s brain development occurs. Their brain acts like a sponge, absorbing everything they see, hear, and experience.  

 Key Takeaways from this session:

Observation Over Lectures: Children in this phase do not learn from lectures; they learn by observing your behavior. If they see respect and patience at home, they adopt it; if they see shouting, they normalize it.   

Time Over Material Gifts: Expensive toys, gadgets, and AC rooms do not guarantee a successful life. Your child craves your undivided attention, deep conversations, and active playtime.  
 
Crucial Skill Building: Outdoor play naturally develops problem-solving skills, while listening to stories builds language and communication abilities.   

Common Mistakes to Avoid: Stop handing them a phone the moment they cry, reducing conversation time because you are busy, and comparing them to other children.   

The 20-Minute Rule: Dedicate at least 20 minutes daily to distraction-free playtime, reading books, pretending, and building an emotional connection with your child.   

These first 7 years won't dictate if your child becomes a doctor or an engineer, but they will decide if they become a confident, kind, and emotionally strong adult. You don't need to provide a perfect environment—just a caring and loving one.

Parents often operate from a place of intense protection. When they imagine you stepping out, their minds immediately rush to, "What if something goes wrong?" or "What if they get hurt?" They aren't trying to ruin your social life—they are just terrified for your safety. But because they only express that anxiety as a strict "NO," it just feels like rejection and distrust to you.  

 It’s time to bridge this communication gap. Teens, understanding the emotion behind the "No" is your first step. Parents, expressing your fears instead of just laying down rules can change everything.  

 Share this with your parents or your teenager, and let's start a real conversation! 👇

 Let us know in the comments: do you struggle with this in your house?

**Parenting ke wo sabak jo kitabon mein nahi milte | Part 2 | Age 4–10 Years | Emotional & Practical Parenting Tips**

Parenting is not just about teaching children what is right and wrong. It is about building a connection so strong that our children feel safe coming to us, even when life gets difficult. ❤️

In this video, I’m sharing some **emotional and practical parenting lessons for children aged 4–10 years** — lessons I have learned through my own parenting journey, which no book could have taught me quite the same way.

✨ **In this video, you will learn:**

* Practical parenting tips you can apply in your everyday life.
* How to understand your child's emotions and respond with empathy.
* How to build a deeper emotional connection with your child.
* How to handle everyday parenting challenges without turning everything into a battle.
* Why listening, trust, and emotional safety matter more than simply expecting obedience.
* How the connection we build during childhood can make parenting during the teenage years easier.
* How to raise emotionally secure children who feel comfortable sharing their thoughts, struggles, and mistakes with us.

**Why start now?**

The teenage years don't suddenly begin at 13. The foundation of trust, communication, and emotional connection is built much earlier. When children feel heard and understood between the ages of 4 and 10, we create a relationship that can help them navigate the challenges of adolescence with greater openness and confidence.

Remember, our goal isn't to raise children who always obey us. It's to raise children who trust us enough to talk to us — even when they disagree with us.

If you're a parent of a child aged 4–10, I hope these lessons help make your parenting journey more meaningful, connected, and a little easier. 💛

recent_videos.title: The Best Preschool Curriculum Isn't a Curriculum
recent_videos.description:
The best preschool curriculum isn't something you buy. 👇

Think of your toddler as your apprentice.
🍳 In the kitchen? Get them in the kitchen.
🥕 Chopping vegetables? Let them chop.
⛽ Getting gas? Let them help fill the tank.

Then talk them through it: what you're doing, and WHY.

👀 Let them see it ✋ Let them touch it 👂 Let them hear it ❓ Welcome every "why?"

That's how kids build the vocabulary that sets them apart. Most kids just aren't spoken to.

It's not a preschool curriculum. It's a LIFE curriculum. And the best person to teach it is the one they spend all day with: you.

Want help building this into your days?

recent_videos.title: Doing everything for your kids isn't good for them or you
recent_videos.description:
Piano, parkour, chemistry, art and a museum trip, all fighting for the same three afternoons.

Every one was genuinely good. That was the problem.

She wasn’t protecting her kids’ opportunities by refusing to cut anything. She was protecting herself from the guilt of being the mom who said no.

So we ran every activity through her family’s Foundation, the three things they said matter most. Two stayed. Three left.

Try it on your own calendar. For each activity, ask:

Does it serve one of our top three priorities?
Would we sign up for it again today?
What does it cost us in time, money and margin?

If an activity fails two of the three, it goes.

Every change is an exchange, never just an addition.

Can’t name your three priorities? That’s the real problem, and it’s where I start with every family. Comment MAP and my team will help you build yours.

#homeschool #homeschoolmom #homeschoolschedule #homeschoollife #christianhomeschool

recent_videos.title: Montessori Explained  #montessori #parentingtips
recent_videos.description:
“The greatest sign of success for a teacher is to be able to say: the children are now working as if I did not exist.” — Maria Montessori

What did she actually mean by this?

In Montessori, success doesn’t look like a teacher at the front of the room directing every moment. It looks like children who are focused, self-directed, and working independently — because the environment and the guidance were so well prepared that they no longer need constant direction.

The teacher’s success isn’t measured by how much they do. It’s measured by how much the children can do without them.

recent_videos.title: Can Mirrors Harm Your Baby? 5 Benefits of Mirror Play for Development
recent_videos.description:
Have you heard that showing a mirror to your baby can cause developmental delays, brain damage, delayed teething, or poor eyesight? These are common traditional beliefs, but there is no scientific evidence that simply showing a baby a mirror causes these problems.

Dr. Anuradha, Pediatrician from Bengaluru, explains why mirror play can be a fun part of your baby’s development.

**5 benefits of mirror play for babies:**

1. **Encourages visual awareness:** Babies enjoy looking at faces, including their reflection, as they explore what they see.
2. **Supports communication:** Smile, talk, and make sounds with your baby while looking in the mirror to encourage interaction.
3. **Introduces emotional expressions:** Make gentle, playful facial expressions to help your baby observe different expressions.
4. **Encourages movement:** Reaching toward a mirror during supervised play can support movement and coordination practice.
5. **Strengthens bonding:** Sharing smiles, sounds, and playful moments helps build connection between you and your baby.

**How to make mirror play safe:** Use a securely mounted, baby-safe mirror, supervise your baby closely, and include mirror play during tummy time only when your baby is awake and supervised.

Remember, mirror play is not a requirement for development, but it can be an enjoyable way to interact with your baby.

Save this reel for the next time someone says, “बच्चे को मिरर मत दिखाओ!” Share it with parents who may have heard this myth.

5 Nuts for Babies: When to Introduce Them & How to Prevent Choking
recent_videos.description:
Can babies eat nuts before their first birthday? Yes! Once your baby is around 6 months old and ready for solids, age-appropriate forms of nuts can be introduced safely. You don’t need to delay them until 1 year without a medical reason.

Dr. Anuradha explains how to introduce nuts while reducing choking risks and supporting your baby’s nutrition.

5 nutritious nuts to introduce in safe forms:

1. **Almonds (Badam):** Provide vitamin E and magnesium.
2. **Cashews (Kaju):** Contain magnesium, zinc, and copper.
3. **Walnuts:** Provide omega-3 fatty acids.
4. **Pistachios:** Contain protein and fibre.
5. **Peanuts:** Provide protein and healthy fats.

How to serve nuts safely:

- Never give whole nuts or hard nut pieces to babies and young children because they can cause choking.
- Use finely ground nut powder mixed into porridge, cereal, or a suitable purée.
- Smooth nut butter should be thinned with water, breast milk, formula, or another suitable food. Never offer thick spoonfuls of nut butter.
- Introduce one new allergenic food at a time, in a small, age-appropriate amount, when your baby is well. Watch for reactions.
- If your baby has severe eczema, an existing food allergy, or a previous allergic reaction, consult your pediatrician about introducing nuts, especially peanuts.

**Know the warning signs:** Hives, swelling, repeated vomiting, coughing, wheezing, or breathing difficulty may indicate an allergic reaction. Breathing difficulty or swelling of the tongue or throat requires emergency medical attention.

Remember: Don’t delay unnecessarily, never serve whole nuts, and introduce them in safe forms.

recent_videos.title: Baby Refusing Frozen Breast Milk? 3 Mistakes to Avoid Before You Throw It Away
recent_videos.description:
Is your baby refusing frozen breast milk? Don’t throw away your entire freezer stash just yet! Dr. Anuradha explains 3 common mistakes to avoid when handling stored breast milk.

**1. Don’t automatically assume the milk has gone bad**

Stored breast milk can sometimes develop a soapy or metallic smell or taste because of an enzyme called lipase, which helps break down fats. This doesn’t automatically mean the milk has spoiled. However, smell and taste alone cannot guarantee safety, so always follow recommended breast milk storage guidelines.

**2. Never microwave or boil breast milk**

Microwaving can create hot spots that may burn your baby, and overheating can damage some of breast milk’s beneficial components. Thaw frozen milk in the refrigerator or under lukewarm running water. Gently swirl the container to mix the separated fat, and check the temperature before feeding.

**3. Don’t routinely heat freshly expressed milk before storing it**

Scalding breast milk to reduce lipase activity is not routinely necessary. If your baby repeatedly refuses previously frozen milk, speak with a lactation consultant or pediatrician before trying this approach.

**Important breast milk safety reminders:**
- Never refreeze breast milk once it has completely thawed.
- Use thawed milk within the recommended time limits.
- Discard leftover milk according to current breast milk handling guidance.

recent_videos.title: Postpartum Back Pain? 5 Nutrition Mistakes New Moms Should Avoid
recent_videos.description:
Experiencing back pain after delivery? While postpartum back pain can have several causes, including muscle strain, posture changes, and physical recovery after childbirth, adequate nutrition is an important part of recovery.

Dr. Anuradha shares 5 dietary practices to help new mothers support their recovery and bone health.

**1. Include protein in your meals**

Protein supports muscle repair and recovery. Include foods such as dal, paneer, eggs, chicken, fish, or sprouts according to your dietary preferences.

**2. Get enough calcium**

Calcium supports bone health, especially during breastfeeding. Include milk, curd, paneer, ragi, and sesame seeds in your diet.

**3. Pay attention to vitamin D**

Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium. Ask your healthcare provider whether you need a vitamin D test or supplements.

**4. Don’t neglect iron**

Iron helps replenish iron stores, particularly after blood loss during delivery. Include iron-rich foods such as leafy greens, legumes, and meat if you eat it. Take iron supplements when recommended by your doctor.

**5. Avoid restrictive diets**

Your body needs enough energy and nutrients to recover after childbirth. If you’re breastfeeding, your nutritional needs may increase. Avoid crash diets and focus on balanced, nourishing meals.

Remember, no single food or diet can cure postpartum back pain. If your pain is severe, persistent, or worsening, consult your healthcare provider to identify the cause. Take calcium, iron, and vitamin D supplements according to your individual medical needs rather than automatically taking them throughout breastfeeding.

Comment **“PAIN”** to get Dr. Anuradha’s diet chart for postpartum recovery.

recent_videos.title: What Should my baby be eating? Episode 3 -Fruits
recent_videos.description:
Banana and apple aren’t the only fruits your baby can eat after turning 6 months!
- Kiwi, strawberries, oranges, papaya, mango, pear, chikoo and watermelon  among others are all fruits you can introduce as your baby begins complementary feeding.
- Don’t limit your baby to just a few familiar fruits. Offering a variety exposes them to different flavours, aromas and textures.
- The key is how you prepare and serve the fruit, not simply which fruit you choose.
- Try mashed banana, ripe papaya, mashed kiwi, soft mango, or soft-cooked apple and pear.
- Depending on your baby’s developmental readiness, fruits can be mashed, puréed, grated appropriately or offered as soft, easy-to-manage pieces.
- Remove seeds, pits and tough peels where needed, and avoid hard chunks or round pieces that could pose a choking risk.
- You don’t need to add sugar or honey to make fruits sweeter. Let your baby explore their natural flavours.
- And remember, whole fruits in age-appropriate textures are a better choice than fruit juices.
Variety matters, but safe preparation and texture matter just as much when introducing fruits to your baby.

recent_videos.title: Postpartum Back Pain & Sciatica: 3 Mistakes to Avoid + A Simple Exercise
recent_videos.description:
Is your wife experiencing severe back pain or shooting pain down her leg after childbirth? Don’t ignore persistent or worsening symptoms, as they may be related to sciatica or another condition.

Dr. Anuradha, Senior Pediatrician from Bengaluru, shares practical tips to help new mothers manage back discomfort after delivery.

3 habits to change after childbirth:

1. Avoid hunching while breastfeeding: Sit comfortably with back support and pillows, and bring your baby to your breast instead of leaning forward.
2. Lift your baby carefully: Bend your knees, keep your baby close to your body, and ask for help with heavy household tasks.
3. Avoid prolonged inactivity: Once your doctor says it is safe, start gentle walking and appropriate movement.

Try the Figure-of-Four Stretch

Sit upright in a stable chair with both feet supported. Place one ankle over the opposite thigh and gently lean forward until you feel a mild stretch. Hold briefly, then return to the starting position. Stop if it causes pain, and check with a healthcare professional before trying it if you have significant postpartum pain.

Important: Seek urgent medical attention for new bladder or bowel control problems, numbness around the groin, or progressive leg weakness. Persistent severe pain, tingling, or numbness also needs medical assessment.

recent_videos.title: Autism & Wrong Answers #autismparenting#autismspeech#executive functioning
recent_videos.description:
Paraphasia (word substitutions) in autistic children 🧠

What it looks like: your child says “pencil” for pen, “sit” for chair, “dog” for cat. A related word comes out in place of the exact word.

Why it happens: the brain stores words in networks. When your child sees a pen, related words come up with it: pencil, write, paper, school. Executive functioning then selects the one that fits the situation. Many autistic children and children with ADHD find this selection step difficult. They know the word, but a related one comes out.

What you can do

1. Avoid saying “wrong.” Model the correct word naturally. Child: “pencil.” You: “Yes, a pen. We write with a pen.”
2. Offer a choice of two. “Do you want water or juice?”
3. Give time for processing. Pause and let your child retrieve the word before you step in.
4. Notice the connection your child made. It tells you how their language network is organised.
5. Work on executive functioning skills: daily routines, visual schedules, sorting objects into categories, games where they choose between options, and “what else can we call this?” play.
#autisticspeech #autismparenting #speechtherapy #autismindia #executivefunctioning

recent_videos.title: 3 Silly Speech Games | Autism, Apraxia & Gestalt Learners
recent_videos.description:
ACTIVITY SHEET ⬇️
1️⃣. Temperature Play (Cold Spoon, Warm Spoon)
Keep two spoons ready, one in the fridge and one in a cup of warm (never hot) water. The parent touches them to the child’s hand, cheek, tummy, or toes, and the child reacts. Then make it a guessing game: the child closes their eyes and decides whether it’s cold or warm before the spoon lands, then predicts where it’s going next. Swapping roles is the best part, because the child gets to tickle the parent.

Goals
1 : “brrr,” “cold,” “hot/warm,” “again,” “more,” plus body-part words (hand, toe, nose).
2: “Cold spoon on my tummy,” “I want warm spoon.”
3: predicting and explaining (“I think it’s cold because it was in the fridge”), comparing (“The cold one is tickly, the warm one is cozy”).
4. Apraxia: "hisss" “brrr” is a lovely lip-and-voice sound, easy to imitate, and the dramatic reaction gives lots of natural repetitions.

Caveat: use the fridge, not the freezer, because frozen steel can stick to skin. Test the warm one on your own wrist first. Some autistic children are touch-sensitive, so start on their hand and let them control where it goes.

2️⃣ Silly Spoon Mistakes
The parent “feeds” a stuffed toy, but gets it wrong on purpose. A shoe on the spoon, a crayon, a toy car. The child’s job is to catch the mistake and fix it. Kids absolutely love correcting adults, and it creates real reasons to speak. Kids find it funny when you say "yucky" and 'spit' it far away too. 

Goals
1: “no!”, “yuck,” “shoe,” “eat,” “stop.”
2: “No, not shoe!”, “Bear wants rice,” “That’s not food.”
3: reasoning and categories (“We can’t eat a shoe because it isn’t food,” “What does the bear really like?”).
4: Apraxia: “no” and “uh-oh” give huge payoff for easy sounds, and the humor keeps repetition from feeling like drill.

recent_videos.title: Approach & assess with care #autism #parentchildconnection #autismmom#autismassessment#autismtherapy
recent_videos.description:
Use your clinical judgment. 👩‍🔬

Documenting support areas is important. Needing deficit information to avail school support and health services is important. But assessment can be more than just that.

For example:

👶 Parent: “He isn’t talking yet.”
Instead of “When was his first word? When did he combine two words?” — find out what he understands, how he communicates without words, what he can imitate, what’s the sound repertoire.

👧 Parent: “She doesn’t interact with other children.”
Instead of “Does she take turns? Does she share? Does she initiate?” — first understand what social communication currently looks like for her. Does she notice people? Share enjoyment? Respond when someone joins her? What happens during play?

the parent sitting beside us isn’t hearing these difficulties for the first time.

They already know.

They live with them every day.

What they may not know is what those difficulties mean, why they are happening, what their child is actually capable of, and what they can do next.

Don’t just tell a parent:

“Your child can’t do this yet.”

Help them understand:

“Here’s what I noticed.”
“Here’s what your child understands.”
“Here’s where they’re struggling.”
“Here’s what might be making this difficult.”
“And here’s what we can work on.”

recent_videos.title: Is Autism Genetic? #autism #autismmom
recent_videos.description:
1️⃣ What can actually cause autism?

• Genetic factors — the biggest contributor to autism
• Rubella infection during pregnancy — can cause congenital rubella syndrome, which is linked with autism
• Valproate exposure during pregnancy — linked with autism

Autism is complex and there is usually no single cause we can point to.

2️⃣ What can increase the chance of autism?

• Having an autistic sibling
• Older parental age
• Prematurity
• Low birth weight
• Severe birth complications
• Maternal diabetes during pregnancy
• Some prenatal exposure to air pollution or heavy metals
• Some medicines taken during pregnancy

These factors may contribute, but they do not explain autism in every child. (World Health Organization)

3️⃣ What does NOT cause autism?

❌ Vaccines
❌ Screen time
❌ Parenting
❌ Bad parenting
❌ A lack of affection
❌ Diet
❌ Sugar
❌ Something the child did after birth
❌ A mother’s emotional stress during pregnancy

recent_videos.title: What we see on the outside is language — words, sentences, questions, answers.
recent_videos.description:
What we see on the outside is language — words, sentences, questions, answers.

But underneath every conversation, there is a lot happening.

A child may need to:

→ Pay attention to what the other person is saying
→ Hold information in working memory while thinking about an answer
→ Understand the question and work out what information is being asked for
→ Find the right words to express an idea
→ Plan and organise those words into a sentence
→ Think about another person’s perspective
→ Solve a problem when communication breaks down
→ Use emotional language to understand and explain how they feel
→ Be flexible when the conversation doesn’t go the way they expected

This is why a child can know the words but still struggle to use them in conversation.

And this is also why we don’t teach all of this by simply asking more questions.

At home, you can support these skills by:

→ Use multiple ways to teach: say it, show it, act it out, use a picture, and let your child experience it.

→ Reduce the memory load: instead of giving 3 instructions at once, give one step, let them do it, then add the next.

→ Give thinking time: ask a question and wait. Don’t immediately repeat it or give the answer.

→ Model the language you want: instead of asking, “Why are you upset?”, model, “You’re upset because the game ended.”

→ Talk through problems together: “The tower fell. Hmm… what can we do now?”

→ Teach language for real situations: “I don’t like that,” “Help me,” “I need a break,” “What happened?” “What should we do?”

→ Talk about thoughts and feelings during everyday life: “I thought it would rain, but it didn’t.” “I think she’s upset because her toy broke.”

The goal isn’t just more language.

It’s helping your child use language to think, solve problems, understand people and share their world.

recent_videos.title: How to support play and why they matter 👇
recent_videos.description:
How to support play and why they matter 👇

🧩 Solo play
• Helps children regulate and recharge.
• Builds attention and independent problem-solving.
• Gives you clues about their interests—your best starting point for language.

👫 Parallel play (playing beside your child without taking over)
• Reduces pressure to interact.
• Helps your child become comfortable sharing space with another person.
• A perfect opportunity to model language naturally without expecting a response.

🤝 Interactive play
• Builds turn-taking, shared attention and flexibility.
• Teaches children that communication changes what happens next.
• Keep it playful, not performance-based.

🏃 Movement play
• Jumping, swinging, climbing, chasing…
• Helps many autistic and ADHD children regulate their bodies before they’re ready to engage.
• Regulation is often the first step to communication.

🎭 Pretend play
• Builds imagination, flexible thinking and understanding different perspectives.
• Creates natural opportunities for rich language.
• It develops differently for every child, so don’t rush it.

💡 A few play shifts that make a big difference
• Follow your child’s interests before introducing your own ideas.
• Ovserve their play before trying to teach.
• Comment more than you question.
• Aim to make your child laugh more than you aim to make them talk.

You don’t have to stop playing to start teaching.

Play is already teaching. The goal is to recognise those opportunities and learn how to build communication through them, not instead of them.

recent_videos.title: Parents are often told, “Talk to your child more.”
recent_videos.description:
Parents are often told, “Talk to your child more.”

So they do this:

“What’s this?”
“What colour is it?”
“Who is that?”
“What did you eat?”
“What’s the animal’s name?”

But here’s what I notice in therapy.

Sometimes I’ll watch a parent interact with their child for five minutes…
…and they’ve asked 40 questions.

Do you know how many complete language models the child heard?

Maybe five.

Every question is a missed opportunity to give language instead of asking for language.

For example…

Instead of:
❌ “What did you eat at school?”

Try:
✅ “I wonder if you had rice today. I packed your lunch, I put lots of yummy mango in it.”

Now your child hears:

* wonder
* today
* packed
* lunch
* yummy
* mango

One question became five or six new language models.

Instead of:
❌ “What colour is your car?”

Try:
✅ “Your tiny blue car is driving so fast! Oh no… it crashed!”

Instead of:
❌ “Where’s the ball?”

Try:
✅ “The ball rolled under the sofa. Let’s look together.”

Instead of:
❌ “What are you drawing?”

Try:
✅ “You’re drawing a huge dinosaur! It has such a long tail.”

Here’s the shift I want parents to make:

When your child already knows the answer…
…don’t ask.

Tell. Describe. Wonder. Predict. React.

Because children can’t learn language they don’t hear.

And if most of your talking is asking questions…
…your child is hearing far less language than you think.

recent_videos.title: Integrated Skills in English Language Teaching (ELT)
recent_videos.description:
Hello,
Integrated Skills in English Language Teaching (ELT) is one of the most widely used approaches in modern EFL classrooms. In this video, you'll learn what integrated skills are, why they are important, and how teachers can effectively combine listening, speaking, reading, and writing to create meaningful learning experiences.

In this video, you'll discover:

👌🏻what integrated skills are .

👌🏻Why integrated skills are essential in language learning 

👌🏻The advantages of integrating the four language skills 

👌🏻Practical classroom examples 
 
👌🏻The relationship between integrated skills and communicative language teaching 

Whether you're an English teacher, student teacher, TESOL/TEFL trainee, or education researcher, this video will help you better understand one of the most important approaches in language teaching.

👍 If you found this video helpful, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to support the channel.

Having children can change your relationship in ways you never expected. 

But feeling disconnected after having children doesn't necessarily mean something is wrong with your marriage. It may mean your relationship needs the same intentional care you give everything else in your life.

In this video, I explore why couples drift apart after becoming parents and what emotionally intelligent couples do differently to protect their connection.

In this video, you'll learn:
* Why couples can feel emotionally distant after having children
* Whether a drop in relationship satisfaction is normal
* Three habits emotionally intelligent couples practise to stay connected
* The biggest mistake couples make when distance begins to grow

You don't need grand romantic gestures to rebuild connection. Sometimes, it begins with being curious about your partner again, repairing after conflict, and making a little space to truly listen.

Want to go deeper?

recent_videos.title: WHAT WORKS FOR HER MAY NOT WORK FOR YOU 😢 | A Powerful Life Lesson#shorts
recent_videos.description:
Bisi watched her neighbour, Mama Grace, making money from selling food and assumed she could achieve the same success. She sold everything in her plastic goods shop and started selling food, believing money would come easily.
But reality taught her a painful lesson.
An elderly woman helped her understand that she had seen Mama Grace’s success but had never seen her struggles, sacrifices, and years of hard work.
The lesson? Don't compare your journey with another person's success. Learn from others, appreciate what you have, and discover what works for you.
Everyone has a different journey, different strengths, and different opportunities. Never abandon your own path simply because someone else's life looks better.
Watch till the end and share this story with someone who needs this reminder.
Vivian Stories — Stories That Touch the Heart.
WhatWorksForHer #VivianStories #LifeLessons #AfricanStories #NigerianStories #MotivationalStory #StopComparing #InspirationalStories #BusinessLessons #ShortFilm

recent_videos.description:
He told his girlfriend that his wife was nothing more than his roommate. He promised her marriage, kissed her hand, and made her believe she was the woman he truly wanted.

But when his pregnant wife suddenly appeared, everything changed. The same man who had promised her heaven and earth suddenly called her a stranger!

Shocked and heartbroken, she finally realised the truth: she had been believing the promises of a man who was already deceiving his own wife.

Ladies, please open your eyes! When a married man tells you his wife is only his roommate, don’t just believe his words. Watch his actions.

If he can deceive the woman he married, what makes you think his promises to you are different?

Watch till the end and share this story with someone who needs this reminder.

What happens when the man you love has nothing to offer you but his dreams?

Tony was intelligent, hardworking, and full of ideas, but life seemed determined to keep him down. With no parents, no money, and no one to turn to, his dreams slowly became a painful reminder of everything he could not provide.

Grace chose to stand by him despite her mother’s warnings. But as poverty tightened its grip on their family, even their love was pushed to its breaking point.

When hunger, humiliation, and hopelessness threatened to destroy everything they had built, Tony began to wonder if his life would ever change.

Then, through an unexpected encounter, a new opportunity appeared.

THE MAN WHO HAD NOTHING is an emotional Nigerian drama about love, sacrifice, poverty, determination, faith, and the power of never giving up.

Sometimes, the person everyone looks down on is only one opportunity away from changing their story.

Watch until the end, and tell us what you would have done in Grace’s position.

recent_videos.description:
What happens when you leave a successful corporate career to become a stay-at-home mom and years later realize you're ready for something more?

In this episode of my Stay-at-Home Mom series, I sit down with Helena to talk about the parts of leaving a career for motherhood that we don't always talk about: identity, financial independence, purpose, being present with your children, and figuring out who you are when one season of your life ends and another begins.

Helena shares what it really cost her to walk away from corporate life, what staying home allowed her to experience with her children, and how she knew when it was finally time to explore something beyond motherhood.

We also talk about how The Makeover Place was born, becoming an entrepreneur after being a stay-at-home mom, and how she now protects herself from recreating the same busyness she once walked away from.

If you're a stay-at-home mom wondering, “What comes next for me?” or a working mom questioning what success should look like in this season, I hope this conversation reminds you that your life can have many beautiful chapters.

In this conversation:
• Leaving a corporate career to become a stay-at-home mom
• Losing financial independence
• Identity after becoming a mother
• Being present during your children's early years
• Knowing when you're ready to work or build again
• Starting a business after a career break
• Motherhood and entrepreneurship
• Redefining success after children
• Finding purpose beyond your previous career

💬 QUESTION: If you've ever taken a career break for motherhood, what was the hardest part of the transition for you and did your definition of success change?

recent_videos.title: I Left My Career To Raise the Children| Was it Worth It? The Truth Every Mom Needs to Hear
recent_videos.description:
What really happens when a woman puts her career on pause to stay home and raise her children and what happens when she's finally ready to return?
In this episode, I sit down with @joan_spaces for an honest conversation about leaving her career to become a stay-at-home mom, navigating the loss of income and independence, wrestling with identity, watching other women progress professionally, and eventually finding her way back into work.
We talk about the beautiful parts of being present with your children, but also the parts of staying home that aren't talked about enough: feeling left behind, questioning your value outside of motherhood, financial adjustments, maintaining your skills and dreams, and wondering whether you'll ever be able to pick up your career again.
Joan also shares how she knew her stay-at-home season was coming to an end, the fears that came with returning to work, how she discovered interior design, and whether knowing everything she knows now she would make the same decision again.
We also tackle a difficult question many mothers wrestle with:
Can you pause a career and come back to it later? And if so, is returning really as easy as people make it sound?
Whether you're a stay-at-home mom who feels invisible, a working mom considering a career break, or a mother who wishes she could stay home but financially cannot, I hope this conversation gives you perspective, encouragement and grace for your own season.

recent_videos.title: From Career to Stay Home Mom to Building a Business While Staying Present With The Children
recent_videos.description:

In episode two of my Stewarding the Stay-at-Home Mom Season series, I sit down with Diana Kagimba, founder of Ruby's Gift Store, to talk about the life she has intentionally built around motherhood, family and entrepreneurship.

Diana shares why she walked away from corporate life, how she and her husband navigated moving from two incomes to one, the reality of adjusting to being home full-time, and why she eventually chose to homeschool her children. But her story didn't stop with staying home. While raising and homeschooling her children, Diana built Ruby's Gift Store and eventually created systems that allow the business to function without requiring her presence in every day-to-day operation.

We talk about how she balances homeschooling, business, marriage, home and herself; what she has had to say “no” to; raising confident and independent children when you're a very present mother; and why she believes children don't necessarily need us less as they grow older, their needs simply change.

We also explore a bigger question: What does it mean for a woman to be fruitful when fruitfulness isn't always measured by a salary, promotion, degree or business?
Whether you're a stay-at-home mom, homeschooling mom, working mother, entrepreneur or simply trying to build a life around what matters most to you, I hope Diana's story gives you something to think about.
